subject: Recap & next steps: Hosted API evaluation and deployment fit
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sue Johnson <sue.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: Hosted API evaluation and deployment fit

Hi Sue / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can get your hosted evaluation rolling: 

Call highlights:
- You want to validate a POC for personalized product recommendations and a support triage assistant.
- Primary constraints: low latency (95p < 300ms for interactive UI), predictable unit cost, and data residency for some EU customers.
- Preferences: start with Hosted API unless rate limits / retention policy force Dedicated or Private VPC.

What I can deliver quickly:
1) Hosted Quickstart pack (attached) — curl examples, sample prompts, and a short sandbox app to hit our public endpoints.
2) Temporary elevated rate key for a 2-week evaluation window so you can load test from your dev/staging traffic.
3) A proposed mutual action plan (attached) that maps checkpoints, metrics, and decision gates (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm preferred evaluation timeframe (2–3 weeks suggested) and whether procurement needs to be looped now.
- We: provision elevated eval key, share quickstart instructions and a sample curl/streaming snippet, and schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Monica for security/retention questions.

Example quick curl (generation endpoint):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer EVAL-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"Recommend 3 products for a user who bought running shoes","max_tokens":120}'

Notes on rate limits & behavior (summary):
- Default Hosted API soft-limits: 60 requests/sec per key, burstable by request for short periods.
- Token throughput depends on model and sequence length; we'll provide an estimate after you share sample traffic.
- Streaming mode supported for interactive UIs to reduce perceived latency.

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

Thanks — happy to iterate on the MAP based on your timeline.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Sue Johnson <sue.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Hosted API evaluation and deployment fit

Rishi —

Really helpful, thanks. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 
- For the Hosted soft-limit you mentioned (60 r/s), is that per API key or per account? Our expected concurrency for peak traffic is closer to 150 r/s if we include background batch calls that drive recommendations.
- Can you confirm typical retention/default logging behavior for Hosted API? We need to know if customer PII is ever logged or stored and for how long; this will gate our procurement team.
- If the Hosted evaluation looks good but we hit rate or residency limits, what is the rough lead time to move to Dedicated capacity?

We attached our security questionnaire (acme-security-questions.pdf) — Monica, could you please take a look when you get a moment?

Tom and I are comfortable starting with Hosted if you can provide an elevated trial key and a short SLA summary for the eval window. Also include a rough token-cost estimate for ~2M tokens across the eval.

Thanks,
Sue
VP Product, Acme Retail
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sue Johnson <sue.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Hosted API evaluation and deployment fit

Sue — thanks for the questions, good points. Answers inline below and next concrete actions at the bottom.

Q: 60 r/s per API key or account?
A: Default is 60 r/s per ingest key. For account-level higher concurrency we can issue multiple eval keys or temporarily raise the account-level soft limit for the 2-week evaluation. Production Dedicated pools provide guaranteed throughput and predictable latency; we can discuss commit sizing if you need it.

Q: retention / logging behavior for Hosted?
A: By default, Hosted API retains logs for 30 days with privacy filters applied; PII is redacted by default unless you opt into longer retention for debugging. For regulated workflows we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed logging. Monica will follow up with the security doc (we received your questionnaire).

Q: lead time to move to Dedicated?
A: Typical lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on GPU sizing and VPC connectivity. For urgent cases we offer a fast-track on-boarding (1–2 weeks) but that requires a committed reservation.

Practical next actions I will do this morning:
- Provision a temporary elevated eval key (60 -> 200 r/s) for 2 weeks and share credentials.
- Add a short Eval SLA note (uptime target for the eval window) — see link below.
- Share a short token-cost back-of-envelope for 2M tokens based on model family (will give low/med/high scenarios).

Monica, could you pick this up on the questionnaire and confirm any gaps for Hosted? If Hosted is blocked we should map the minimum requirements that would force Dedicated vs Private.

Eval SLA link: https://drive.redwood.ai/eval-sla-template (draft)

Attachment: acme-security-questions.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

Best,
Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sue Johnson <sue.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Hosted API evaluation and deployment fit

Thanks Rishi — that sounds reasonable and fast. We accept the 2-week elevated key to stress test. Two quick asks before you provision: 
- Procurement wants a short note on the eval SLA (uptime & support response) to be able to approve the temporary access.
- Can Monica confirm whether Hosted fits our EU data subset (some of our user identifiers are EU-resident)? If not, we may need to prioritize Dedicated or Private.

I'll coordinate on procurement from our side (procurement@acmeretail.com) and propose a check-in on Mon, 2026-02-23 at 10:00 AM PT for the first run review.

Tom
Director of Engineering, Acme Retail
